newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- China and Russia sign joint statement on promoting world multi-polarisation and establishment of new world order.

- Chinese President Jiang Zemin and his Russian counterpart Boris Yeltsin pledge to further strengthen the two countries' strategic coordination partnership of equality and mutual confidence oriented toward 21st century.
- State Council approves new rules on village household registration system
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH

- WTO Director-General Renato Ruggiero says optimistic about China's accession to the World Trade Organisation, says as long as all parties show sense of urgency and necessary flexibility and concentrate on negotiation, they will achieve balance of interest.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- PICC Property automobile insurance premiums hit 21 billion yuan in 1996, up 14.3 percent yr/yr
- PICC Life pays 10,000 yuan compensation to top gymnast Li Xiaoshuang
- State Administration of Foreign Exchange renews licence of Chia Huaneng Financial Co for foreign exchange business
FUTURES HERALD
- Meteorologists say drought occurs in north China

- Official of State Grain Reserves Administration says total losses in state grain dealing sector reach 19.577 billion yuan in 1996, says total grain to be shipped from northeast to reach 15 million tonnes by time new crop arrives
FINANCIAL MORNING POST
- Editorial says conditions ripe for China to set up specialised savings banks
CHINA DAILY
- China plans to launch series of theme tour drives in next three years to attract more overseas visitors
- China will introduce "Ecotourist Tour" in 1999
- Commentary attacks visit by Japan lawmakers to Yasukuni shrine
- State Planning Commission official says China wants more overseas participation in development of energy sector
